MESSAGE FROM THE
CHIEF ELECTORAL OFFICER, MANIPUR

Manipur is a small State where more than 90% of the total area is covered by
hills where 60% of the population is confined to Imphal valley. It is inhabited
by different ethnic groups spread across 16 revenue districts.

Given the presence of difficult terrain, unfavourable law and order
situation, large number of communities spread across the state,
inadequate transport and communication facilities, presence of interest
groups, non-state actors and so on, conduct of Elections in Manipur has
always been a challenging and humongous task. Despite all such
challenges, the election machinery has been able to ensure conduct of
free and fair elections because of meticulous planning in advance,
effective awareness campaigns, rigorous training of all stakeholders and
special emphasis on preventive measures to obviate law and order problems.

lam happy to say that the voters of Manipur have shown umpteen enthusiasm in every elections held in the
past. This time in the 12th General Elections to Manipur Legislative Assembly-2022, the voter participation
reached alltime high recording 90.28% as compared to 86.59% in State Assembly Elections held in the year
2017. Further, under Mission 300 Programme, average voter turnout of the lowest 300 Polling Stations
increased from 62.31% in SAE-2017 to 84.01% in SAE-2022, exhibiting a whopping increase of 21.69%.

lam also delighted to highlight that, 604 all-women polling stations were set up as symbol of women
empowerment which was 1 /5th of the total polling stations. This has been the highest in the country. On the
accessible elections front, | am extremely pleased to say that over 95% of the registered alive 100+electors
participated in voting either through Postal Ballot or by voting on Poll Day. Further, over 90% of the PwD
voters exercised their franchise. Such is the level of enthusiasm of the voters of Manipur irrespective of age,
gender, religion, community when it comes to exercising their voting rights.

| wholeheartedly appreciate all the election machineries including District Election Officers, Returning Officers,
Assistant Returning Officers, BLOs, Nodal Officers, polling officers and all other field functionaries in the district
who had made significant contributions to the conduct of elections. | also thank law enforcement agencies both
at the State and District for their effective management of law and order thereby resulting into a peaceful poll. |
also thank political parties, media houses, CSOs/NGOs, State Icons for their overwhelming cooperation
extended to us in successful conduct of elections. Last but not least, | would also like to express my sincere
gratitude to all the voters of Manipur for exercising their franchise and making a truly participative democracy.

This Statistical Report gives a detailed account of various aspects of conduct of elections to the 12th General
Elections to the Manipur Legislative Assembly including, Polling Stations, Electoral Rolls, EVMs and VVPATs,
IT Applications, Voter Turn Out, Political Parties & Candidates, Expenditure, Model Code of Conduct,
Security, Vehicles, Media, SVEEP etc. The report will be beneficial to all stakeholders including District
Election functionaries, Media houses, political parties and candidates, Researchers and the voters at large.

| wish the readers a very pleasant reading.

Rajesh Agrawal
Chief Electoral Officer, Manipur

preparation of Electoral Rolls. The schedule of the Special Summary Revision w.r.t.
01.01.2022 as the qualifying date is shown below:

During the Revision period, a total of 88,593 electors were added in the
electoral roll. 22,103 number of electors deleted from the electoral roll. There
was a net increase of 66,490 from the draft electoral roll. After the publication
of Final Electoral Rolls on 05.01.2022, updation of electoral rolls continued till
the last date of making nominations. Accordingly, the total number of electors
stood at 20,48,169 at the time of elections.

INCREASE IN THE EP RATIO

Intensive efforts were carried out during the SSR 2022 for enrolment of all
eligible voters. A part wise analysis was done to identify gaps in enrolment.
Wherever shortfalls occur, focused strategies were chalked out. Door to door
survey by BLOs, assistance by BLAs and support of local clubs, village chiefs and
elders were crucial for enrolment of eligible unenrolled voters. Eventually, the EP
ratio increased from 55.8% to 57.70% during the revision period.

INCREASE IN GENDER RATIO ON ROLLS

The participation of women in the electoral process in the State of Manipur has always been

traditionally high. During the revision period, 49464 female electors as against 39100 male
electors were added in the electoral roll. As a result, the gender ratio increased from 1060 to
1065.

INCREASE IN 18-19 YEARS REGISTRATION

A thorough micro level gap analysis was done on the basis of Format 1 to 8 and KAP Survey
to maximise enrolment of 18-19 age group. In addition to door to door survey by BLOs,
efforts were made to identify newly eligible voters in colleges/ universities. Adequate
multimedia campaigns were created during the entire Revision period. The services of
Campus Ambassadors, NYKs were utilized. With the addition of 38481 electors in 18-19
age group, the ratio increased from 0.93% to 2.66%. This is 43% of the total inclusions made
during the revision period.

INCREASE IN REGISTRATION OF PwD

The number of PwD electors marked in the electoral roll was only 7520 in the Final Roll of
2021. The efforts for enrolment/flagging of PwD electors in the electoral roll began during the
Continuous updation. The BLOs were made to visit every household for identification of PwD
electors and facilitate their enrollment in the electoral roll. In addition, the list of PwD electors
were obtained from the Health Department. The Office of CEO also tied up with Handicapped
Foundation, Manipur, one of the leading organisations working for PwD and organized
awareness campaigns across the State. PwD Icons were also appointed both at the State and
District level and their services were effectively utilized in creating awareness. TV discussions,
radio talks were also held extensively. With all these efforts, the number of PwD electors
increased upto 14565 in the Final Electoral Roll-2022 which is an increase of 94%.

EPIC/PER COVERAGE, EPIC DISTRIBUTED IN NATIONAL VOTERS’ DAY
The State has achieved 100% EPIC coverage. The newly enrolled voters were felicitated on

the National Voters Day celebrated in all polling stations. In addition to taking pledge, EPICs
were distributed to all newly enrolled voters.

PARTNERSHIP BUILDING

The Office of CEO, Manipur partnered with the following departments/agencies/NGOs:

Education Department both Schools and Higher Education - for identification and
enrolment of newly eligible voters. Also, active cooperation was extended from the
Departments in ensuring that the polling stations met the required AMFs for creating a
conducive environment for conduct of poll.

8 | STATISTICAL REPORT 2022

Social Welfare Department

The department extended maximum support by providing the services of Anganwadi
workers and helpers in assisting the BLOs and Polling Teams on the day of poll.

Health Department

The Department provided the list of PwD electors and this has enabled the EROs to
enrol/mark in the electoral roll with ease. Besides, the department took up a lot on
initiatives for ensuring a COVID free poll.

Handicapped Development Foundation

The NGO in collaboration with the other NGOs operating in the districts organized a
month long awareness campaign across the State in creating awareness for enrolment of
eligible PwD voters and motivated them to exercise their franchise. Registration/marking of
PwD electors increased from 7520 in Final Roll-2021 to 14565 in Final Roll 2022 and
over 90% of the PwD electors participated in voting either through Postal Ballot or on Poll
Day.

Transgender Organizations

The Transgender Organisations extended an overwhelming support in maximising
enrolment of Transgender electors and their participation in the electoral process. A lot of
awareness campaigns were conducted at the State as well as District level. Transgender
Icons were appointed both at the State and District level and their services were effectively
utilised. The enrolment of Transgender electors increased by 26.8% from 164 to 208.
Over 90% of the registered TG electors cast their votes.

Fluorescence Pvt. Ltd.

The Office of CEO, Manipur tied up with Fluorescence Pvt Ltd, a multi media creative
agency for creating multi media messages in various platforms including Social Media,
Electronic & Print Media, Outdoor campaign etc. with a view to enroll all eligible voters
and motivate them for participation in the electoral process.

Leading Media Houses

The Office of CEO, Manipur also partnered with the Sangai Express, one of the largest
circulated English daily in Manipur. In addition to publication of quarter page/half page
ads on weekly basis on different topics, island ads portraying various messages were
carried out on daily basis. With support from the local dailies, the messages relating to
elections could be percolated down to far flung areas.

text:
SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS, STATE ICONS

The Office of CEO, Manipur appointed 7 State Icons representing various fields including
Sports, Art & Culture, Film, Fashion industry, PwD, Transgender to appeal to the voters of all
segments and ensure 100% participation.

CONDUCT OF ELECTIONS - PEACEFUL AND INCIDENT FREE POLLS

Except for some minor incidents, the General Elections 2022 was largely a peaceful
election. Effective maintenance of law and order, preventive measures including vigorous
Counter Insurgency Operations, frisking and checking, seizure of cash in circulation, seizure
of illicit liquors and banned drugs, disposal of pending cases and NBWs helped us in
peaceful conduct of election. As a preventive measure for ensuring peaceful poll, over 81%
of licensed arms were deposited as against 60% in SAE 2017. Further, 7624 trouble
mongers, history sheeters were bound down. Moreover, 100% of NBWs were executed.
Interestingly, the number of repoll reduced from 34 PS in SAE-2017 to 19 in SAE-2022.

VOTER TURNOUT - OVERALL AND IN LOW TURNOUT AND VULNERABLE PS

A comprehensive SVEEP campaign unleashed for over six months beginning from pre
revision activities till Poll Day through multiple media platforms and series of physical
outreach programs was adopted. Concerted efforts were continuously invoked on voter
awareness for enrolling the unenrolled eligible electors, optimum participation, inclusive
elections, ethical voting, free, fair and peaceful elections, awareness on Voter Helpline App,
PwD App, COVID safe elections, C-Vigil app, KYC App etc. Specific Targets were also
adopted on increase in voter enrolment, voter turnout, marking of PwD electors, categorising
the low voter turn out polling stations and invoking target specific SVEEP interventions to
achieve much higher voter participation, ensuring inclusive election by way of mapping each
PwD elector individually for electoral participation. With all these efforts, the overall voter
turn out reached all-time high of 90.28% in SAE-2022.

Besides, an initiative called Mission 300 was taken up wherein 300 polling stations having
lowest voter turn outs in SAE 2017 were identified and focused booth level strategies were
executed in collaboration with BLOs, local elders etc. Eventually, the average voter turnout of
these 300 PS increased from 62.31% in SAE-2017 to 84.01% in SAE-2022, exhibiting a
whopping increase of 21.69%.

VOTER TURNOUT - MEETING GAPS IN GENDER, URBAN AND YOUTH PARTICIPATION

The participation of female voters in electoral process has always been traditionally high.
However, efforts were made to enhance their participation by making them informed voters.
Intensive awareness programmes were launched including radio ads, TV ads, radio jingles,
street plays, drama etc. in vernacular languages to educate them fo enable them to vote ethically.
As a result, female voter turn out stood at 90.56% in SAE 2022 as against 87.90% for male.

10 | STATISTICAL REPORT 2022

Besides, to address the issues of urban apathy, focused interventions were chalked out.
Adequate awareness campaign were taken up in market areas in coordination with the
shopkeepers associations, Municipal authorities. Posters carrying electoral messages were
pasted in conspiscuous areas, pamphlets were distributed, hoardings were erected. Small
sized ads carrying electoral messages appealing the voters were also attached with
grocery items, LPG cylinders etc to reach out to every household. As a result, the Average
voter turn out in urban areas increased from 84.6 % in SAE 2017 to 89.28% in SAE 2022.

INNOVATION IN PROCESS /PROCEDURE

Intensive efforts were undertaken for advance mapping of every PwD elector, 80+ elector
and Transgender elector and to ensure their optimum participation on Poll day. Every PwD
voter was mapped with a volunteer. Facilities for pick up/drop were provided.

24x7 State Command Centre was set up at the office of CEO, Manipur under the
supervision of State Health Nodal Officer to promptly respond to any casualty/incident.
District Command Centres were also made operational at District level under the
supervision of District Chief Medical Officers. Assembly Constituency level Rapid Response
Team (RRT) were set up with 1 Medical Officer and support staff including nurses and
paramedics. Two Helicopter RRTs service were utilized for emergency casualties for far
flung areas.

INNOVATION IN THE USE OF TECHNOLOGY

Implementation of election e-Atlas system for effective planning and monitoring of poll.
eAtlas which is a GIS based application for reporting of EVM malfunction and for
reporting other incidents, malpractices etc. The application primarily consists of a
Dashboard for use by the Returning Officer/ District Election Officer/Chief Electoral Officer
at the Control Room and a Mobile App to be used by the Presiding Officer at the polling
booth. The Presiding Officer reports EVM malfunction and other incidents through the App
by sending photograph/video along with a description and the same is popped up with an
alarm in the Live Dashboard. From the Control Room, the RO/DEO/CEO addresses the
issues instantly thereby enabling a smooth poll.

As many as 142 incidents relating to malfunctioning of EVMs and other 67 incidents
relating to malpractices were reported and resolved within 10-15 minutes.

ACCESSIBLE ELECTIONS

Over 95% of the registered alive 100+electors participated in voting either through Postal
Ballot or by voting on Poll Day. Each centenarian voter was mapped with a volunteer.
Every centenarian voter was awarded a gift from the Office as a token of appreciation.

Over 90% of the registered Transgender electors participated on Poll Day. Transgender
electors were constantly engaged through various awareness programmes.

Randomization Software for Polling Personnel (RSPP)

The Chief Electoral Officer, Manipur developed a web-based randomization software to cater to the local
requirements as well as need for special cases related to difficult hilly terrain locations of the Polling Station where
dispersal takes place on P-2 or P-3 days. The required age and physical fitness for these polling personnel were
considered.

Key Features & Functionalities

* RSPP applications provide complete functionalities of Randomization viz. Polling Personnel Randomization,
Police Personnel Randomization and Counting Personnel Randomization.

* Centralised hosting is done at National Informatics Centre Manipur State Unit, Imphal. No need to maintain
servers, storage etc., at District level.

* Polling personnel are dispatched two to three days ahead for Polling Station located in difficult hilly terrain.
* Staffs are deployed through three stages of randomization.

* RSPP also provided exemption feature based on medical ground.

112 | STATISTICAL REPORT 2022

Polling Personnel Randomization

2m seem

FIRST STAGE RANDOMISATION LOCK

r ™ \eeexeranan, 200000 | Min

In the first stage, polling parties are constituted randomly with the help of RSPP software. The process
involves randomly picking at least 20% more officers than the required number, then this group is trained
for election duty.

In the second stage, polling parties are formed from this group of trained officials. This process also
involves randomization through RSPP software. However, in the second stage, General Observers
appointed by Election Commission are involved to ensure the integrity of the randomization process.

In the third stage of randomization, polling booths are randomly assigned polling parties just before their
departure. It means, these randomly created polling parties do not know the specific polling booths where
they will be deployed till the time of their departure.

Police Personnel Randomization

Similar three-stage randomization is conducted for police personnel as well.

Counting Officials Randomization
The counting official's randomization is also done in three stages.

In First randomization, a list of 120% of the required number of officials (Counting Supervisors/Counting
Assistants/Micro Observers) required for counting in the district, are generated (including reserve) randomly,
using the RSPP software by the District Election Officers one week prior to the date of counting. Presence of
observers is not required at this stage. This is only to identify and select the officials who would be given duty
for counting as Counting Supervisors/ Counting Assistants/ Micro Observers. In no case, at this stage, the
identity of the assembly constituency to which the Counting personnel are likely to be deployed is disclosed.
The appointment letters are issued by the RO concerned.

The Assembly Constituency wise randomization i.e. Second randomization is done by the District Election
Officers in presence of Observer(s) 24 hours prior to commencement of counting. Thereafter, the Returning
Officer issued the appointment letters to these officials intimating them about the concerned allotted ACs.

In Third randomization, the allotment of counting tables in the counting hall, to the Counting
Supervisors/Counting Assistants/Micro- Observers is done in the presence of EC! Observer at 5.00 AM on the
day of counting.

Mission 300 VOmnES Metiour

Elections in Manipur have always seen active participation from the electors, thereby posting a respectable voter turn-
out percentage. However, due to social, geographical, and logistical challenges, some polling stations receive lesser
voter participation. This has been a consistent trend in almost every election. These polling stations have been lowering
the state vote percentage in every election.

With the objective of addressing this issue and increasing the voter turn-out in these polling stations, the state election
team did a comprehensive brainstorming and came up with a remedial campaign under the name ‘Mission 300'.
Under this campaign, 300 polling stations with the lowest voter participation in the 1 1th State Assembly Elections were
identified. Strategies were made, and plans were drawn to implement them in a systematic and organised manner.

A series of targeted interventions, including awareness programs, regular meetings at various levels, door-to-door
visits, systematic follow-up SOPs and various other activities, were thus undertaken. Arrangements of facilities that
were previously unavailable in these polling stations were considered and put in place to help achieve the goals of
Mission 300. In addition to spreading awareness in the area, there was continuous engagement with them through
booth level WhatsApp groups administered by the BLOs and even relocation of Polling Stations more centrally to
improve access to vote.

This report aims to cover and highlight the various initiatives and activities CEO Manipur implemented under Mission
300 in its collective endeavour to outdo past performances and bring the identified polling stations at par with the state
average.

HEALTH
Major Highlights

* Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) activated in all District Headquarters and Assembly Constituencies for
attending health exigencies

* Training, dry run, evacuation plan etc.

* Command Centres set up at State, District , AC.

* Air ambulance for lifting of casualty polling and security personnel

* 18 injured personnel air lifted in time.

* Cashless treatment provided to all injured security forces and election machineries.

During the conduct of elections, polling parties including the security personnel experience difficulty in
reaching far-flung polling stations. At times of medical needs, they often face tough times in reaching the
nearest health centres in time and sometimes they may be referred to well-equipped health centres for further
treatment which may need immediate attention or may face untimely death. The scenario of COVID pandemic
during the conduct of General Election 2022 was a big challenge for a small hilly state like Manipur. The
safety of the polling personnel and general public was at huge risk.

While keeping in mind the safety of the polling parties and the voters at large, various activities were taken up
in coordination with Health Department. Precautionary doses were provided to all the Polling Personnel and
elderly voters. Providing of Masks, hand gloves, hand sanitisers and ensuring physical distance of 6 feet
among the voters on the day of election were ensured. Steps were also taken to ensure that COVID positive
persons vote at the last hour of voting by providing PPE and transport vehicle to the polling station. Adequate
measures were also taken to provide treatment to injured polling personnel at the quickest possible.
